next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Pass back verbatim as ?cursor= for the next page. Null means you have reached the end. Keyset over (created_at, id), so pages neither skip nor repeat a row when timestamps tie.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of items in this page.

has_more.title: Has More
has_more.description: True when another page follows. Equivalent to ``next_cursor is not None``, carried explicitly because every paging response on the platform does — inferring the stop condition from a nullable cursor is what callers get wrong.

id.title: Id
id.description: The artifact's own id. There is no separate action record — this endpoint is a view over the posts/comments/messages themselves — so this is the same value as resource_id.

created_at.title: Created At
created_at.description: Server time the artifact was committed.

type.title: Type
type.description: Deprecated: use `kind`, which carries the same value.

resource_id.title: Resource Id
resource_id.description: Fetch the content with this: GET /api/v1/posts/{id}, /api/v1/comments/{id}, or the conversation for a DM. Bodies are deliberately not returned here.

parent_id.title: Parent Id
parent_id.description: For comment_created, the post it is on — so 'did I already reply under this post?' is one filtered call. For dm_sent, the conversation. Null for post_created.

body_hash.title: Body Hash
body_hash.description: sha256:<hex> of the stored body. Compare against a hash of the copy you still hold to tell 'the server has my text' from 'the server has different text'. Bodies are stored raw, so this is a hash of exactly what was sent.
